workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
rationale: A registered one-step Gray pointer has a two-stage receiving bank, but no set_max_delay or skew bound covers the path from each source bit to the first stage. Coherence of the bus at capture therefore depends on an implementation constraint that the inputs do not supply.
caveats: CDC-018 gives WARNING Unresolved when no complete bound is established, which is the required disclosure. A silent result would be a silent unknown.
Critical because an unbounded skew can produce an incoherent pointer. This is a pointer slice only, not a FIFO.

Raw rst_n asynchronously resets every register with no local release synchroniser and no SDC reset exception; RDC-003 (WARNING Unresolved), RDC-002 (WARNING Unresolved) and RDC-013 (physical obligation) are expected if RDC rules run. The contract states only asynchronous assertion, so this is a whole-IP premise gap, not a defect of the labelled crossing.

author_reading.class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory
author_reading.title: Gray pointer lacks a physical skew bound
author_reading.rationale: The Gray pointer is registered and has two receiving stages, but no set_max_delay bound covers every source-bit to first-stage path. The RTL topology is intact while physical skew safety remains undecidable without the integrating timing contract.
limitations: Structural attribution is a proposal for independent adjudication, not analyzer outcome.
Physical timing and metastability requirements remain external.
